title: Integrality over affine groupoid invariants
statement: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] are morphisms such that, functorially in every test scheme $H$, $U(H)$ is the object set and $R(H)$ the arrow set of a groupoid with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$ and composition $c$. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp,\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$ and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then $A$ is integral over $C$: every $a\in A$ satisfies a monic polynomial in $C[T]$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-rankwise-monic-gluing] to the given affine groupoid. It supplies the finite invariant rank pieces and the restriction isomorphisms for $A,B,C$. If $U$ is empty, its polynomial $T$ already proves the claim. Otherwise its index set $I$ is nonempty. Fix $a\in A$ and write $a_r$ for its component on $U_r$; each $A_r$ is nonzero and the restricted groupoid has both projections of positive constant degree $r$.

For each rank piece, identify the affine object and arrow schemes with the spectra of their global section rings using Scheme.isoSpec. Naturality identifies the new source and target maps with Spec.map of the original appTop maps. Transport the identity, inverse and composition along these isomorphisms; composition uses the induced map between pullbacks, and each groupoid law follows by cancelling the object or arrow isomorphism and applying the original law. The source and target squares are pullbacks with horizontal isomorphisms, so finite local freeness and fibre degree r are preserved. Nonemptiness of the object piece makes its section ring nontrivial. Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-constant-rank-norm-annihilator] to the transported groupoid and the component a_r. Its canonical polynomial is monic of degree r, belongs to the polynomial lifts of the appTop equalizer inclusion, and evaluates to zero. Choose a polynomial lift; injectivity of the subring inclusion reflects monicity and preserves degree, and evaluation of its coefficientwise image is evaluation through that inclusion. Rewriting C_r by the supplied equalizer equality gives precisely the polynomial required by the gluing statement.

proof.text: Use the common-degree conclusion of [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-rankwise-monic-gluing] for these $P_r$ and $a$. With $d=\max I$, it combines the coefficients of $T^{d-r}P_r$ through $C\cong\prod_rC_r$, producing a monic $Q\in C[T]$ whose value at $a$ has every component zero, and hence $Q(a)=0$. Since $a$ was arbitrary, this is exactly integrality of $A$ over $C$.
